articles.title: High Court Trial Begins Over Ownership of Hopwood Hall
articles.excerpt: A two-day trial in the High Court will determine the future of Hopwood Hall, with Hopwood DePree seeking to reclaim his ancestral home from Rochdale Council.
articles.content_html:
A trial concerning the ownership of Hopwood Hall commenced today in the High Court in Manchester. The case involves Hopwood DePree, a descendant of the family that built the historic manor house in the 1420s, and Rochdale Council, which currently owns the Grade II-listed property.

Mr DePree's claim arises from a legal dispute over an exclusivity agreement he had with the council, which he asserts was violated when the council decided to explore other options for the property in November 2024. This decision followed seven years of collaboration between Mr DePree and the council to undertake essential repairs on the dilapidated site, which is adjacent to Hopwood Hall College.

The Hopwood family owned the hall and surrounding land until 1922, after which it was sold and subsequently used for various purposes, including as a Catholic teacher training college until the 1980s. The council acquired the property after it fell into disrepair.

The outcome of this trial, which is expected to conclude tomorrow, could significantly impact the future of Hopwood Hall and its potential restoration. Mr DePree argues that the council must proceed with the transfer of ownership now that planning permission has been granted.
